summary: New box Imperativ: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (108/16)

data.turoyo: Komər lu waziro məllele: “De xaroṭo, həz iḏux, be lo gqəṭʕat qarʕe du baran!”
data.translation: Da sprach der Wesir zu dem Schreiner: Fang an zu sägen, ob du nicht den Kopf des Steinbockes abschneiden kannst.

rationale: First Imperativ box; the craft addressee and explicit hand object anchor the work instruction.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC NE Farrucke/6)

data.turoyo: Hizola, hizola, hizola, baq+qudrat d Aloho, hawyo k̇ačk̇e.
data.translation: She rocked her, rocked her, rocked her, by the power (lit. ‘powers’) of God, she became a girl.

rationale: Unusual feminine patient before feminine agent, with lexical repetition; cradle-rocking is absent from the five inherited Preterit contexts.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC NE Old woman and a fox/30)

data.turoyo: Veǧa kuzzé, maʕ+ʕəšqat kohōz hawxa ruḥe, kəmmi ‘xəng xəng xəng xəng’. Kuzzə́n aḥ+ḥawronayḏe li+qamaytayḏe.
data.translation: Then he is leaving, he is quivering with joy like so, they go ‘jingle, jingle, jingle, jingle’. His friends come out to face him.
data.ref: MAC NE Old woman and a fox/30

rationale: Unusual contracted hōz with an overt reflexive; compare the full inherited hayzat ruḥax.

evidence.cite: MAC NE Old woman and a fox/30

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC NI Fingan Agha and Sultan Hasan/60)

data.turoyo: ‘Ohooo’, kohṓz qarʕe Ṣәlṭā́n Ḥasan, kohṓz qarʕe.
data.translation: ‘Ohoooo’, Sultan Hasan shakes his head, he shakes his head.
data.ref: MAC NI Fingan Agha and Sultan Hasan/60

rationale: Second contracted hōz context, contrasting masculine head movement with the full hoyəz base.

evidence.cite: MAC NI Fingan Agha and Sultan Hasan/60

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (95/106)

data.turoyo: Hano, Ḥasana Aliki, barəm ḥeḏ̣ər di kone w ʕal aš šalite di kone w gmihozo i kone me raġloṯe di səsto, Genǧ Xalil Aġa maḥəsle.
data.translation: Ḥasan Aliki ritt um das Zelt herum, über die Zeltstricke hinweg. Da kam das Zelt durch die Füße der Stute ins Schwanken, und Gendsch Chalil Agha wachte auf.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Infectum cell; tent swaying with an explicit me-marked cause.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (115/69)

data.turoyo: Hawi komər hul li saʕaye ʕaṣro, Baṣuṣ daməx, u abro du malko taʕobo yo, u yawmo kule kəmhalxi, koməhne ʕal as səsye, ha komihəz, nayəs w daməx.
data.translation: Es wurde gegen zehn Uhr, Basus schlief, er ist ja Prinz, er ist müde. Den ganzen Tag waren sie auf den Pferden geritten, er hatte sich schütteln lassen; er war schläfrig geworden und schlief ein.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Infectum cell; involuntary bodily shaking during riding in a past narrative.

summary: New idiom: həzle/hoyəz iḏe 'Hand anlegen, sich an die Arbeit machen'

data.headword: həzle/hoyəz iḏe 'Hand anlegen, sich an die Arbeit machen'
data.turoyo: De xaroṭo, həz iḏux, be lo gqəṭʕat qarʕe du baran!
data.translation: Fang an zu sägen, ob du nicht den Kopf des Steinbockes abschneiden kannst.

rationale: One attestation, hand movement directed to a named craft task. Conventionality remains an editorial question; no matching input lookup.

summary: New idiom: həzle/hoyəz u zago di xwazginiye 'die Glocke der Brautwerbung schwingen'

data.headword: həzle/hoyəz u zago di xwazginiye 'die Glocke der Brautwerbung schwingen'
data.turoyo: Komər azzeyo. Həzle u zago di xwazginiye.
data.translation: Er ging hin und schwang die Glocke der Brautwerbung.

rationale: Repeated culturally specific collocation at 61/317 and 62/48,53,110; search found no registered match. Retain the edition’s literal gloss.

summary: Physical shaking, swinging and rocking cover people, limbs, weapons, bells, cradles and ropes. Nodding is already explicitly represented; motion direction and assent do not justify additional senses.

Active hyz plus ruḥe/ruḥax contrasts with Detransitive mihoz- motion in 36/119 and the MAC contracted hōz example. Detransitive subjects include the cave, a head, supporting wood, hands, a tent and a rider; no omitted external agent is required in every case.

Contracted kohōz/kohṓz contrasts with hoyəz/hayz-. In the Preterit, hizola orders the feminine patient vowel before the female agent suffix. Repeated predicates remain individually counted but yield one quotation.
The Preterit həzle in 108/5 appears in a prospective temporal condition; the Infectum also occurs in past narrative settings. Do not determine the box from German tense.
Military mobilisation is already inherited at LB 334. New fieldwork source Talay 1/334 confirms the same passage, so the reader’s proposed new figurative sense is merged.

Hand-as-work instruction and courtship-bell movement are recorded as collocations. Only the former has one attestation; the latter recurs across several Ritter passages. Neither creates a numbered sense.

Both occurrences are I Preterit sense 1 physical head movement. Assent follows from the adjacent good/truth statements and is already represented by inherited nodding examples, not a new numbered sense.

No added example: R1 already leaves six Preterit contexts and covers head-shaking, nodding and morphological contrasts. The proposed better-context addition offers no clear improvement over the existing self-contained dialogue.
Is həz iḏux conventionally “get to work”, or a literal craft-specific hand-movement instruction? The single attestation is marked as a proposed collocation.
Check initial ḥ in PrS 6/40 ḥəzle and PrS 11/12 Kḥoyəz against the edition; do not merge homonymous ḥyz by spelling alone.
Resolve hoyazno u taxt di xwazginiye in 96/197 against German sitting on the courtship seat. No new sit meaning is accepted.
Verify numbering concordances for inherited Prym–Socin citations and LB 334/Talay 1/334 before rewriting those citations.
Handshaking, moving stirrups and shaking a signalling rope retain physical movement; no participant-specific sense is required.
Military mobilisation is an established figurative use already illustrated in the entry; the new source confirms it.
Kopfbewegung mit zustimmender Rede bestätigt den bereits vorhandenen Gebrauch; Jan 2.12/2946 hat qarʕe als Körperteilobjekt und lu ḥasyo als L-markierten Agens neben -le.
